threadSnapshot.title: withCacheIsolation declares a synchronous result but always returns a Promise
threadSnapshot.body:
Hullo folks,

I’m doing some research for Tessl Code Review and ran it against your repo. It flagged a potential issue, and I figured it made sense to share it with you:

## Describe the bug

`withCacheIsolation` is exported with return type `T`, but its implementation is always async. For a synchronous handler returning `Response`, the public type therefore permits `result.status` and `result.headers.get(...)`, while the actual result is a Promise. The first access returns undefined and the second throws.

Expected: the wrapper’s call signature exposes `Promise<Awaited<ReturnType<T>>>` (while retaining applicable copied properties), so TypeScript requires awaiting this result. Normal H3 route dispatch already awaits handlers; this report concerns direct consumers of the public helper.

## Environment

Current main: 2f29b875617e8daf39d25118f7474fd4c24fbfe1 (package.json: h3 2.0.8), Node.js 25.2.0, macOS 27.2 arm64. Executed the current source with srvx 1.0.6; no HTTP server or external service required.

## Reproduction

In a checkout of the commit above, with its runtime dependencies installed, save this as `repro.ts` at the repository root and run `node repro.ts`:

```ts
import { withCacheIsolation } from "./src/utils/cache.ts";
import { H3Event } from "./src/event.ts";

const event = new H3Event(new Request("https://example.test/"));
const result = withCacheIsolation(() => new Response("ok"))(event);
console.log(result instanceof Promise, result.status);
console.log((await result).status);
console.log(result.headers.get("content-type"));
```

The unwrapped handler returns a Response; awaiting the wrapped result also gives status 200. Direct access through the declared synchronous result fails.

## Logs

```text
true undefined
200
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')
```

## Additional context

This finding comes from [Simon’s retrospective Tessl review of merged PR #1608](https://github.com/sjmaple/cr-h3/pull/10#discussion_r4327620094), followed by the current-source reproduction above. It was also [flagged in the original upstream review](https://github.com/h3js/h3/pull/1608#discussion_r4326313968); I did not find a separate tracking issue or subsequent fix. This is a reproducible follow-up to that unresolved point, not a claim that it was first discovered here.

Validation was limited to the current helper and its actual event/dependencies under Node; I have not run the whole test matrix or proposed an implementation change.

Full transparency: I work at Tessl, and we've spotted that using Tessl Code Review -  using repository-level context and specific review lenses that improve over time through feedback. That’s how this finding surfaced.

We’re just getting started and want to offer the tool free to open-source projects. If this is useful, happy to give you access.

Bap

threadSnapshot.title: fix(cache): type the `withCacheIsolation` result as a promise
threadSnapshot.body:
Resolves #1670

`withCacheIsolation` was typed to return `T`, but the wrapper is async, so a synchronous handler's result came back as a Promise while the type said otherwise.

The returned handler is now typed as `(event: H3Event) => Promise<Awaited<ReturnType<T>>>`, and keeps the properties of the wrapped handler (such as ocache's `invalidate`) through `Pick<T, keyof T>`. No runtime change.

Added type tests for a sync and an async handler and for a copied property. `pnpm typecheck`, the type tests, the cache and route rules tests, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm build` pass.
